part.text: {"items":[{"index":1,"kind":"reframe","meets_criterion":"yes","quote":"evaluate independent fine time-slices in parallel as GPU batches, then iterate the time grid until the trajectory correction converges","reason":"Parareal computes fine time-slices across many timesteps simultaneously, then iterates corrections; the step-after-step time dependency is removed."},{"index":2,"kind":"reframe","meets_criterion":"no","quote":"Reformulate the algorithm as tiled wavefront kernels on a GPU: process anti-diagonals of tiles, keep boundary cells in shared memory","reason":"Reformulates the fill so tiles within each anti-diagonal run at once, but each diagonal still waits on the previous one."},{"index":3,"kind":"copies","meets_criterion":"no","quote":"Run thousands of independent chains in lockstep GPU batches; vectorize the target log-density over chains and data","reason":"Thousands of independent chains run side by side; each chain still advances one accept/reject step at a time."},{"index":4,"kind":"other","meets_criterion":"no","quote":"Use a fixed-step GPU loop with parallel neuron updates, delayed ring buffers for spikes, atomic synaptic accumulation","reason":"The timestep loop stays sequential with delayed spike delivery; only neuron updates within each step are parallel — single-step splitting, not copies."},{"index":5,"kind":"reframe","meets_criterion":"yes","quote":"split the time domain into chunks run on separate GPU streams or tiles, solve corrections on a coarse time grid","reason":"MGRIT computes time-domain chunks simultaneously and iterates coarse-grid corrections, removing the serial one-timestep-at-a-time march."}]}
